questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q:
Observe the following statements
i. The dipole moment of $\mathrm{NH}_3$ is higher than the dipole moment of $\mathrm{NF}_3$.
ii. The dipole moment of chloroform is zero.
iii. Covalent bond character in $\mathrm{NaCl}$ is more compared to $\mathrm{CuCl}$.
questions.solution:
Only statement (i) is correct.
- i. The dipole moment of \($\mathrm{NH}}_{3}\) is higher than the dipole moment of \( \mathrm{NF}$}_{3}\). This is correct. In \($\mathrm{NH}}_{3}\), the bond dipoles of the three \( \mathrm{N}-\mathrm{H}\) bonds and the lone pair on nitrogen all point in the same general direction, adding up to a larger net dipole moment. In \(N F_3\), the bond dipoles of the three N-F bonds point towards the highly electronegative fluorine atoms, while the lone pair dipole points away. These dipoles oppose each other, resulting in a much smaller net dipole moment.
- if. The dipole moment of chloroform is zero. This is incorrect. Chloroform (\(\mathrm{CHCl}$}_{3}\)) is a tetrahedral molecule with three highly electronegative chlorine atoms and one less electronegative hydrogen atom. The bond dipoles do not cancel each other out, resulting in a significant net dipole moment.
- iii. Covalent bond character in NaCl is more compared to CuCl . This is incorrect. According to Fajan's rules, a smaller cation with a pseudo-noble gas configuration (like \(C u^{+}\)) has a greater polarizing power than a cation with a noble gas configuration (like \($\mathrm{Na}^{+}$\)). This increased polarizing power leads to a greater covalent character. Therefore, CuCl is more covalent than NaCl.

Thus, the correct statements are a, b, and c.
